note: From the original Latin description by Silvestri 1923 (as the new species Hamitermes excellens sp. nov.); the species was later placed in Amitermes. In this reading only the first half of the alate description was available (head, antennae, pronotum, body colour) together with the plate captions (figs. 8—11 show the soldier head, labrum and legs); the soldier text was not within this window, so no soldier section is given.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original was published as the new species Hamitermes excellens. The alate head is slightly longer than wide and wider than the distance between the compound eyes, the vertex with short hairs, the fontanelle large and nearly oval, slightly longer than wide; the postclypeus is distinctly inflated and hairy, its half about 1/4 longer than wide; the compound eyes are rather large and projecting, the ocelli small; antennae 15-segmented.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Colour: head and postclypeus brick red, the mouthparts and the tergite of abdominal segment 10 pale red, the sides of the sternites brown, the remaining surface pale milky white, legs pale red, wings brown. Head slightly longer than wide and wider than the interocular distance, dorsally with short hairs and denser, shorter hairs; fontanelle large, nearly oval, slightly longer than wide; postclypeus distinctly inflated and hairy, its half about 1/4 longer than wide; compound eyes rather large, convex, projecting; ocelli small, their distance from the compound eye slightly less than the longitudinal diameter of the ocellus; antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 about half as long as segment 2 and about 1/3 shorter than segment 4, segment 4 slightly longer than segment 5. Pronotum slightly narrower than the head (including the compound eyes), its anterior margin not concave in the middle.
